title: Seven Big Countries Tell Iran: Stop Arming the Houthis in Yemen
summary:
Imagine a doorway so narrow that ships carrying oil and toys and food all have to squeeze through it. That doorway is called the Bab al-Mandab Strait, and it sits between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. This month, a group called the Houthis took control of it.

Now, seven big countries — the United States, the UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, and Japan — have a message for Iran. They say Iran must "end its arming of and support" for the Houthis. Iran says it never gave the Houthis weapons and only supports them politically.

The G7 also said it strongly condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia backs Yemen's government, and the two sides have been fighting hard. The Houthis have fired drones and missiles at Saudi cities, including the capital, Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has hit back with hundreds of air strikes.

Why does this matter to you? The Bab al-Mandab is a gateway for ships that carry goods around the world. If fighting blocks that route, prices for things like fuel could go up everywhere. The United Nations says more than 120,000 Yemenis have been forced to leave their homes. Thousands have fled across the Red Sea.

The G7 statement came just before a big meeting in New York called the UN General Assembly, where Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, is set to speak.
why_it_matters: A fight in a faraway waterway can still change the price of fuel and food where you live, because so many everyday goods travel by ship through narrow sea routes.

background_read: Yemen (a country at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula) has been torn by war for years, after the Houthis — a rebel group that took over the capital — fought the government.

Saudi Arabia (a large oil-producing country next door) leads a group of countries that back Yemen's government, which is why Houthi drones and missiles often target Saudi cities such as the capital, Riyadh.
The G7 (the seven big economies that signed the message) often makes joint statements when its members want to put pressure on another country.
The United Nations General Assembly (a yearly gathering in New York where leaders from almost every country give speeches) is a common moment for leaders to talk about conflicts like this one.
Article_Structure: WHO: The G7 countries (the United States, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan), Iran, the Houthis, Saudi Arabia, and Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian.
WHAT: The G7 told Iran to 'end its arming of and support' for the Houthis and condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; Iran denies giving the Houthis weapons.
WHERE: The Bab al-Mandab Strait between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean, Yemen and Saudi Arabia, and the UN General Assembly in New York.

WHY: The strait is a gateway for ships carrying goods around the world, so fighting there can raise prices everywhere, and the United Nations says more than 120,000 Yemenis have been forced to leave their homes.

perspectives.description: They say Iran must stop arming and supporting the Houthis, and that attacks on Saudi Arabia must be strongly condemned.
Iran insists it never gave the Houthis weapons and says it only supports them politically.
The United Nations reports that more than 120,000 Yemenis have been forced from their homes, and thousands have fled across the Red Sea, so ordinary families pay the heaviest price.
